classification.difficultyReason: Combine isosceles and exterior-angle reasoning, express two lengths using right-triangle ratios, then use the prompted results in AB/BC and cancel x to prove the identity.

content.prompt: The triangle $ABC$ is right angled at $B$. Suppose that $AD=DC=x$ and $\angle ACB=\alpha$.

spec.description: Right triangle ABC with D between B and C, internal segment AD, a right-angle mark at B, alpha at C, and single equal-length ticks on AD and DC. Both equal segments are labelled x.
spec.mathematics: AB is perpendicular to BC; B, D and C are collinear; AD=DC=x; angle ACB=alpha. Construction coordinates enforce the equal lengths.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens remain visible; no derived lengths or angles are supplied.

answer.short: Since $AD=DC$, $\angle DAC=\angle ACD=\alpha$. The exterior angle $\angle ADB=\alpha+\alpha=2\alpha$.
answer.worked:
Since $AD=DC$, triangle $ADC$ is isosceles, so $\angle DAC=\angle ACD=\alpha$. As $DB$ extends $DC$, the exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ADB&=\angle DAC+\angle ACD\\\angle ADB&=\alpha+\alpha\\\angle ADB&=2\alpha.\end{align*}$$

Using parts (b) and (c) in right triangle $ABC$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\alpha&=\frac{AB}{BC}\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{x\sin 2\alpha}{x+x\cos 2\alpha}\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{x\sin 2\alpha}{x(1+\cos 2\alpha)}\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{\sin 2\alpha}{1+\cos 2\alpha}.\end{align*}$$
